Background / Context

The project involves developing a content management system (CMS) tailored for Ruby on Rails developers. Refinery CMS is designed to create customizable and content-manageable websites efficiently by adhering to "The Rails Way." It is well-suited for developers familiar with Ruby on Rails and aims to streamline the development process.

Objectives

- Provide an intuitive CMS for building and managing websites.
- Simplify content creation and management with visual tools.
- Support easy customization through extensions and plugins.
- Facilitate secure user authentication and role management.
- Enable seamless integration of media files and resources.

Stakeholders & Users

- Developers: Primarily Ruby on Rails developers who will implement and customize websites using Refinery CMS.
- Administrators: Users responsible for managing website content, structure, and user access.
- End-users: Individuals who will interact with the front-end of websites built on Refinery CMS.

Functional Descriptions

1. Page Management: 
   - Edit and organize pages using a visual editor.
   - Manage site structure and navigation.

2. Media Management:
   - Upload and insert images seamlessly using Dragonfly.
   - Store media on Amazon S3 for scalability.
   - Manage and link to various resources such as PDF documents.

3. User Authentication & Roles:
   - Manage user access and roles using Devise.
   - Define permissions for extensions and functionalities per user.

4. Extension Support:
   - Generate custom extensions using the Refinery extension generator.
   - Popular extensions include:
     - Blog: Manage posts, categories, and comments.
     - Portfolio: Create image galleries.
     - News: Post and manage news items.
     - Inquiries: Handle contact form submissions and notifications.

Non-Functional Descriptions

- Ease of Use: Designed to be approachable for Ruby on Rails developers, leveraging Rails conventions.
- Scalability: Supports scalable media storage with Amazon S3 integration.
- Security: Secure authentication and role management using industry-standard practices (Devise).
- Extensibility: Easily extensible through generators and available plugins.

-- Schema for database: schemabench_0006
CREATE TABLE `admin_users` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `role` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `email` (`email`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `blog_categories` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `blog_posts` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `content` text NOT NULL,
  `category_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `category_id` (`category_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `blog_posts_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`category_id`) REFERENCES `blog_categories` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `blog_comments` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `content` text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `post_id` (`post_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `blog_comments_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`post_id`) REFERENCES `blog_posts` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `extensions` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `extension_users` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `extension_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `user_id` (`user_id`),
  KEY `extension_id` (`extension_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `extension_users_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `admin_users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `extension_users_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`extension_id`) REFERENCES `extensions` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `inquiries` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `message` text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `media` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `file_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `file_type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `file_path` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `news` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `content` text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `pages` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `content` text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `portfolio` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `image_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `image_id` (`image_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `portfolio_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`image_id`) REFERENCES `media` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `roles` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `user_roles` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `role_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `user_id` (`user_id`),
  KEY `role_id` (`role_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `user_roles_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `admin_users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `user_roles_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`role_id`) REFERENCES `roles` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `users` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `email` (`email`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `website_structure` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `page_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `parent_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `page_id` (`page_id`),
  KEY `parent_id` (`parent_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `website_structure_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`page_id`) REFERENCES `pages` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `website_structure_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`parent_id`) REFERENCES `pages` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
